_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-25 · A long working session with Sam driving COBI in a browser and reporting things as he hit them. Almost everything found was a real defect rather than a preference. The Memory tab's status chip appeared to do nothing: the instruction that saves a change was addressed by a name that six entries simply do not have, so those saves quietly matched nothing and the page blamed an expired team phrase instead. Once that was fixed the chip turned out to step through the statuses in a fixed loop — and every step it passed through was really saved, so getting an entry to 'stale' recorded a verification along the way that nobody had made. One entry still carries that false mark. Signing in by email link always returned you to the Common Course Reference no matter where you started, for everyone, because the note saying where you were is kept in a place a newly-opened browser tab cannot see. On SkyView, searching for a subject spelled three slightly different ways sent you to an unrelated subject entirely; the search now offers suggestions as you type. And the GR Priorities tab can now be edited row by row, with an on-demand re-check of each item's legal citations before anything goes to the Chancellor's Office.
_status: Two releases went out today. The first is live: the sign-in state now shows at the top of every COBI screen, and Memory entries can be marked inactive, restored or deleted. The second is waiting on its tests and carries the SkyView search fixes, the Memory status menu, the email-link return fix, and the new GR Priorities editing. The one genuinely unfinished thing is on GR: none of the twenty regulation revisions has had its legal citations checked against the primary source yet, and that is curator work rather than something the software can do. For a draft going to the Chancellor's Office this week, that is the number worth moving.

items.text: Open a regulation priority, edit it, and press Re-analyze. The check is deliberately not an opinion — it tells you which sections your text cites that are missing from the citation list, which listed ones the text no longer mentions, any section number that is ambiguous between two codes, and any section another priority area is also proposing to change. It checks the row against itself, not against the law.

None of the 20 regulation revisions has had its citations confirmed against the primary source — 0 of 20. For a draft going to the Chancellor's Office this week that is the number to move, and only a person can do it. Each row has a 'Mark citations verified' button.

Say whether to clear one entry that is marked stale but still carries a verification stamp — it was recorded by the old status chip while stepping past 'verified', not by anyone actually checking it. Eleven other entries carry a person's name as verifier while still proposed; those are real and must not be touched.

Some CPL regulation rows are already set to 'anyone in the CO' rather than MAP team only. Our notes said nothing was open yet, which turned out to be wrong. Worth a look before anything is exported, because the 'not yet verified against the source' caveat travels with the Word file.

Decide whether you want drafting help for the 'Why it matters' text and the priority ranking. It is not built. It would need a change to the assistant's server, which is deployed separately from the site and is shared with the public assistant, so it is a deliberate step rather than a small one.

Open the Common Course Reference. It now shows the map first, with the list a button away. Try typing a subject name — suggestions should appear as you type — and try 'Browse subjects as a list', which now gives you an actual filterable list of all 302 subjects instead of the work-packaging screen it used to open.

Build the grouped work surface for every subject, not just 5 of 159 — about 1% of the corpus. It is the bottleneck behind every other improvement to that tab. It is too big for one file, but the code already fetches course descriptions one subject at a time, so the pattern exists.

Work the 73 course-control numbers that genuinely point at two different courses. They sit at 12 colleges and 93 of the rows are at San Jose City College alone, so it is one conversation more than it is a project.
Twenty-six memory entries are marked verified but name nobody as the verifier. New verifications now record the signed-in person, so this is a backlog rather than an ongoing leak.

Cañada College still renders with a mangled name in SkyView's member list. The name-folding rules exist but the member list never consults them, and the source export carries only the broken spelling — 678 times — so it needs repair at source.

The My College entry in the project notes has grown past its size budget and now states several generations of findings at once. It should be cut back to what is currently true, with the history moved to that workstream's lessons file.
